name: Sendinês (Mirandese meridional)
notes: Sendinês subdialect of Mirandese, spoken in Vila de Sendim (southern extreme of Terra de Miranda). It inherits the full Central Mirandese system (graphemes_base=mwl: apical ⟨s⟩ /s̺ z̺/ vs predorsal ⟨c,ç,z⟩ /s z/, ⟨x⟩ /ʃ/, ⟨j,g⟩ /ʒ/, ⟨ch⟩ /tʃ/, ⟨nh⟩ /ɲ/, nasal-vowel digraphs) and overrides only the two documented Sendinês deltas: (1) monophthongisation of the Leonese diphthongs ⟨iê/ie⟩ → [i] and ⟨uô/uo⟩ → [u] (tirra not tiêrra, curpo not cuôrpo): the Central [jɪ]/[ʊ] is reduced to [i]/[u]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §50, p. 219) gives "fierro / firro" and §58 (p. 226) gives "bọ̌no / buno", "olho / ulho". (2) The Latin initial L stays [l] where Central Mirandese has [ʎ] (lhado → lado, lhuç → [ˈlus]): §111 (p. 259), "O L inicial latino mudou-se normalmente no mirandês central ou normal em lh; no sendinês porém conservou-se". Medial ⟨lh⟩ stays [ʎ]: LdV gives Sendinês ulho (p. 226), so only a word-initial ⟨lh⟩ is [l] (positional entry). Disagreement: the Primeiro Aditamento à Convenção (February 2000), as secondary sources report it, has Sendinês depalatalise every ⟨lh⟩ (alá for alhá, lhobo → [ˈlobu]), and the mirandese_g2p row alhá → [ɐˈla] follows it. The mirandese_dict rows tagged Sendinês keep the medial [ʎ] (olho → [ˈoʎu], mulher → [muˈʎeɾ]). LdV does not say that the medial [ʎ] is lost, so the spec keeps it. The Aditamento also lets Sendinese writers spell word-initial ⟨l-⟩ (not ⟨lh-⟩). The unstressed vowel qualities are inherited from Central Mirandese, where they are grounded in Leite de Vasconcelos's description of Duas-Igrejas (unstressed ⟨o u⟩ = [u], unstressed and final ⟨e⟩ = [ɨ]). Whether Sendinês realises those unstressed vowels differently is not settled by any description reached so far, and the Sendinês gold sample is too small to decide it; the inherited Central values stand until a published source says otherwise. SENDINÊS -ien. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §50, p. 220, Obs. 1): "Quando porém o ĕ latino se torna nasal e final, o sendinês offerece íẽ (com accento tonico no i)", with quíẽ, cíẽ, bíẽ. The three words are word exceptions, [ˈki.ẽ], [ˈsi.ẽ] and [ˈbi.ẽ], because the syllabifier counts ⟨ie⟩ as one syllable and so cannot place the stress on the i. His footnote says that the final vowel is hard to tell from the neighbouring nasal vowels because it is unstressed, "por isso escrevi simplezmente ẽ", so the spec writes the plain nasal [ẽ]. Central quien and bien are the diphthong ẹ̌ (quĩẹ̌̃ p. 220), which has no spelling difference from the Sendinês words. A written final ⟨ie⟩ is [i] (positional entry): §56 (p. 225) gives tìệ as "em sendinês ti" and frìệ as "em sendinês fri". The word exceptions tue, sue, ũa, ũas, algũa and algũas, and non, repeat the central values (see the notes of mwl). ENDING "on" is [ɐ̃w̃] (Vasconcelos 1900, vol. I, §110, footnote: "Em sendinês parece que se diz -ão, ex.: rõuquidão, satisfação, como em português"), and ENDING "ion" is [jɐ̃w̃] for the same reason (Vasconcelos 1900, §110). The footnote is hedged ("parece"), and it is the only statement of a Sendinês -on.

allophone_rules.notes: Sendinês has the high central nasal [ɨ̃] in unstressed word-final -en, where central Mirandese has the mid central [ə̃]. Leite de Vasconcellos (1900, vol. I, §77, p. 239): "A -em atono no fim de palavras corresponde em mirandês normal -ḙ̃ e em sendinês -ẽ̥", with amen → amẽ̥, amassem → amassẽ̥, têem → tenẽ̥, devem → debẽ̥, and "o send. ẽ̥ representa uma das phases intermedias entre -ent e -ḙ̃". The ring below marks the "e surdo" [ɨ] (§24, p. 201: "i. é, e surdo (= e̥) nasal").

stress.notes: Convenção Ortográfica da Língua Mirandesa (1999) accentuation, Portuguese-based: paroxytone default; written accent (acute or tilde) overrides. Oxytone-attracting endings reflect Mirandese orthography: consonant-final r/l/z/ç (rapaç, Pertual, falar) and the final nasals written with -n in the Asturleonese manner — -in (camin, Sendin), -un, and the systematically oxytone -on class from Latin -ōnem (naçon, coraçon, Associaçon). Unmarked -an/-en verb endings stay paroxytone as in Portuguese -am/-em. Dialect mwl-x-sendim: no evidence of stress-pattern divergence from standard Mirandese; block copied from mwl (cliticless_words included, since stress is not inherited). Sendinês has [l] for an initial ⟨lh⟩ by its own positional entry and monophthongises ⟨ie⟩→[i]; quien, bien and cien are word exceptions with the stress on the i. The article l is a word exception that MWL_ARTICLE_L_VELAR velarises before a consonant.

mirandese_g2p.measured: The mirandese_g2p row holds 11 gold pairs, per=0.3258, per_ci_low=0.1641, per_ci_high=0.4824 (benchmarks/results.json). The 95% interval includes 0.25, so the row cannot be read as a failure. The parent mwl spec's own mirandese_g2p row draws on the same underlying source with 205 pairs and measures per=0.1317, well under the threshold; the 11-pair Sendim subset is too small to show whether it genuinely differs from that larger measurement or is simply noise (audit is OWN_ONLY and is not inherited from mwl).
